addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- codex:codex-rescue: Proactively use when Claude Code is stuck, wants a second implementation or diagnosis pass, needs a deeper root-cause investigation, or should hand a substantial coding task to Codex through the shared runtime (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)
- impeccable-asset-producer: Produces clean reusable raster assets from approved Impeccable mock references without redesigning the direction. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep)

- impeccable-documenter: Records DESIGN.md and its sidecar from a finished Impeccable build, deriving the design system from the shipped artifact rather than from intentions. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Glob, Grep)

- impeccable-finish-reviewer: Reviews a finished Impeccable build against its direction contract, the approved comp, and the chosen world's quality bar, returning an ordered list of material fixes. (Tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep)

## claude.ai HyperFrames by HeyGen

[HeyGen HyperFrames MCP] — Programmable HTML video projects.

## When to use this MCP

This MCP is the primary HyperFrames surface for hosted chat clients (Claude.ai
web/desktop, ChatGPT, Grok, and similar), where the user has no local filesystem
and the agent cannot author HyperFrames code directly.

From a CLI/IDE agent on the user's machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, the
localhost MCP Inspector, etc.), **`compose` and `render_video` are disabled** — these clients have a local
filesystem, so author HyperFrames with the local HyperFrames skills instead, which
produce standalone HTML compositions the user can edit, diff, and commit. Calls to
those two tools from such clients are rejected with a pointer to install them:

    npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes

The read tools (list_projects, get_project, get_project_status, get_render_status)
stay available to every client.

After installation they expose slash commands like `/hyperframes` (compose),
`/hyperframes-cli` (init, lint, preview, render), and `/hyperframes-media`
(TTS, transcribe, remove-background). See
https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes for the full skill list and docs.

But the skills and this MCP are *not* drop-in equivalents:

- Local skills → standalone HTML/GSAP files on disk. No `project_id`, no hosted
  artifact, no integrated cloud render pipeline.
- This MCP → hosted HeyGen project with a `project_id`, a live canvas at
  `app.heygen.com/projects/{id}`, and the cloud render queue.

Route by what the user actually wants:
- "Make a local HTML composition / something I can edit" → use a local skill.
- "Make a HeyGen project I can share / render in the cloud / open in the app"
  → use this MCP, even from a CLI agent.

## What it does

HyperFrames is HeyGen's framework for creating, editing, and rendering programmable
HTML-based video projects. Projects are authored interactively (Magic Edit
chat-driven flow) and rendered to MP4, WebM, or MOV at any framerate. Tools exposed
here cover composing, listing, fetching, and rendering projects… [truncated]

## zotero-research
Read-only access to the user's Zotero research library. For substantive sport-science questions, build a Zotero-first evidence pack before answering. Return bounded page-located evidence, label external fallback sources explicitly, and never represent a Reference Stub as a reviewed Paper Brief. SecondBrain Queue is the priority lane; promotion eligibility is controlled by promotion_scope.

1	# Sources and gap analysis
2	
3	Compiled 2026-10-04 by a research pass over the SSI material, the 9/9 webinar, Eric's
4	March drafts, the Software & Technology framework, and UT's policies. Read-only; no
5	source was changed. Main finding: the Software & Technology framework fully carries only
6	SSI Rec 4. The registry note overstated the rest, and **no source addresses
7	staff-transition continuity** (see D).
8	
9	Drive folder below = `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\01_PROJECTS\_STALLED\2026-03-05_SSI_PerformanceTechRecs\`
10	Framework = `~/DEV_archive_hold/2026-10-03/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/` (archive hold until 2026-11-02; repo on GitHub, archived)
11	
12	## A. Source inventory
13	
14	| Source | What it is | Status |
15	|---|---|---|
16	| Drive `SSI_PerformanceTechRecommendations.pdf` | NCAA CSMAS/SSI, "Performance Technologies Recommendations: Responsible Use in Collegiate Athletics", 5 pp, March 2026, from the May 2025 Summit | Read in full |
17	| Drive `SSI_Notes_09092026.docx` | Fireflies-style notes on the 9/9 webinar, organised by theme | Read |
18	| Vault `Inbox/meetings/2026-09-09_NCAA_SSI_Webinar__Performance_Tech__Data_Governance.md` | Summary and action items only | Read |
19	| Fireflies transcript `01M23EEHZ3CRE03AYYADWA3N0D` | Full 45-min SSI Spotlight webinar | Read in full. A keyword search returned 0 results, but a date-range listing found it. |
20	| Drive `NCAA_Performance_Tech_Action_Plan_DETAILED.docx` | March 2026, roughly 7.5k words: Baylor roadmap per recommendation, with templates (charter, consent form, access matrix, checklist, surveys) | Read |
21	| Drive `NCAA_SSI_Summary_and_Recommendations.docx` | Memo dated 7 Mar 2026 with a 4-phase plan (Mar → Fall 2026) | Read (some sentences truncated in the source) |
22	| Drive `NCAA_PerformanceTech_Condensed_v2.docx` | 1-page table: each recommendation, then a Baylor action | Read (text garbled in places) |
23	| Drive `SSI_PerformanceTech_StaffOverview_v3.md` | Marp staff deck, April 2026 | Read |
24	| Vault `Inbox/meetings/2026-05-26_Athlete_Data_Legal_Discussion.md` | Summary of an outside-counsel discussion (proposal for phased policy, vendor-risk, SOP and training work) | Summary only. No transcript found. |
25	| Framework `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-04-…design.md` | Design document | Read |
26	| Framework `deliverables/Software_and_Tech_Management_EXEC_SUMMARY_ER_2026-08-14.docx` and `Software_and_Tech_Management_ER_2026-08-14.docx` | 2-page summary and full draft | Read |
27	| Framework `docs/TALKING_POINTS_ER_2026-08-13_internal.md` | Internal talking points | Read |
28	| Framework `UT_Technology Policies and Procedures/` SMED-8055 policy, PROC-SMED-8055, SMED-8110 | Peer examples | Read |
29	| UT `Human Performance Release.pdf` | Scanned image. A 2015-dated **assumption-of-risk / liability waiver**, **not** a data-consent form. | Viewed |
30	
31	UT's policy lists a "Student-Athlete Informed Consent Form – Performance Technology Use",
32	but that form is not in the folder.
33	
34	## B. SSI recommendations (PDF structure)
35	
36	The PDF uses three kinds of statement (p1, Fig. 1): **Foundational**, **Recommendation**
37	and **Strategy**.
38	
39	**Foundational statements (p2)**
40	- **Fundamentals.**
41	  - Performance technology is defined broadly: "devices that enable users to collect and record biometric and/or performance data", including "cameras, sensors, surveys, software, mobile apps".
42	  - It is "just one tool".
43	  - Quality varies (accuracy, reliability, validity, function) and should be assessed "prior to selecting or implementing".
44	- **Rights and Protections.**
45	  - Schools need to understand "student-athlete rights and protections" and "applicable local and international laws".
46	  - Unintended impacts "including implications for mental health" matter.
47	- **Written Plan.** Covers how groups are educated, how data is managed, how purchase and implementation decisions are made, and how continuous improvement works.
48	
49	**Rec 1 – Policy (p3).** Establish a written plan.
50	- 1.1: a multidisciplinary team develops, "routinely" reviews and revises it (student-athletes, sports medicine, coaches, athletics administration, legal affairs, IT).
51	- 1.2: address school-specific considerations.
52	
53	**Rec 2 – Education (p3).** "Education is foundational for informed consent."
54	- 2.1: "At least once annually" for anyone selecting, using or accessing data.
55	- 2.2: tailor by group (student-athletes, coaches, S&C, sports medicine, administration).
56	- 2.3: topics are limitations and harms; data privacy and security; student-athlete rights ("e.g., informed consent"); departmental policies.
57	
58	**Rec 3 – Data Management (p4).** Establish "who owns data… where and how data is stored,
59	who has the authority to access data and how data is permitted to be used", working with
60	legal and risk management.
61	- 3.1: who may interpret and communicate data, with "required competencies and oversight".
62	- 3.2: what rights, "if any", the school has over collection, use, access and ownership, "including considerations for transfer student-athletes".
63	- 3.3: permissible uses. Sports medicine must be involved when data informs medical decisions, preserving the "unchallengeable, autonomous authority" of primary healthcare providers over return-to-play.
64	
65	**Rec 4 – Selecting and Implementing New Technologies (p4).** A structured decision process.
66	- 4.1: evidence-based standards for value, usability and quality.
67	- 4.2: assess accuracy, reliability, validity and function.
68	- 4.3: a multidisciplinary group decides (sports medicine, sport science, coaching, IT, data security, administration, compliance).
69	
70	**Rec 5 – Continuous Improvement (p5).** Get feedback "routinely" and revise the plan.
71	- 5.1: a multidisciplinary group, ideally including the plan's authors.
72	- 5.2: student-athlete feedback is "critical".
73	- 5.3: feedback from other groups on implementation, effectiveness and education.
74	
75	The PDF does **not** mention vendor contracts, NIL, research use or staff turnover.
76	
77	## C. Webinar takeaways (9/9 SSI Spotlight)
78	
79	Speakers: the SSI moderator "Dina"; Tim Coffey, Longwood (FAR, biomechanist; the
80	transcript renders "Crockey"); Mark Koberly, Iowa State Sr. Assoc. AD (the notes spell
81	it "Coberly").
82	
83	**Consent**
84	- **Mark (21:34):** athletes "should have the right to not participate." Some data is unavoidable (venue tracking), but "a wearable… would require their consent", and consent "is one of the things that probably most people are not doing."
85	- **Tim (02:47):** the summit's origin was athletes opting out of research because "I don't want the number in my head."
86	- **Mark (34:16):** athletes should be told when their de-identified data goes to vendor norm-building.
87	
88	**Data ownership and privacy**
89	- **Tim (30:13):** "talk with your general counsel".
90	  - State laws vary, and HIPAA has "real exclusions".
91	  - Staff treat this data as postable "in a locker room" or usable "as part of a broadcast".
92	  - De-identification fails: with a roster of 13–14, "I can probably identify which athlete's which".
93	  - Cloud storage risk.
94	  - Settle access "on the front end before we start collecting".
95	- **Mark (34:16):** physiological data (HR, HRV) is "more likely to be HIPAA protected" than performance data (40-yard time).
96	- **Tim (39:45):** "if you're not doing anything with it, don't collect it" (the IRB minimum-data principle).
97	
98	**Vendor contracts**
99	- **Moderator (33:09):** vendors offer "a discount if you sell back some of your data". Purchasers may not grasp it, and sports medicine "may not be aware that that is even part of the contract".
100	- **Mark (34:16):** vendors commonly pool de-identified data "to start developing norms". Involve legal and IT.
101	- **Moderator (36:16):** add campus risk management.
102	
103	**NIL / pay**
104	- **Mark (34:16):** "now that we're paying players… there's going to be a bigger concern" about data use. He cited pro-league player-association rules as precedent.
105	
106	**Turnover.** Athlete turnover only, not staff. **Tim (38:38):** "with the transfer portal, rosters change over even faster", so feedback and norms need re-checking.
107	
108	**Governance and adoption**
109	- **Mark (10:16 / 13:37):** purchases driven by "fear of missing out". Start from the question. Be "data guided, not data driven". Iowa State built "more procedures" than policy, plus an intake **form** asking about validity, reliability, use, access and ownership.
110	- **Mark (17:35):** two risks: failing to act on critical data, and misuse or misinterpretation.
111	- **Mark (26:22) / Tim (29:10):** "black box algorithm". Two devices gave "completely different scores" on the same workout, and four published equations exist for one metric.
112	- **Mark (42:10):** value means ROI; re-evaluate "if we're not acting on the data".
113	
114	**Mental health**
115	- **Tim (19:05):** a rugby "data surveillance" study, and staff who could not define acceleration.
116	- **Mark (26:22):** leaderboards.
117	
118	## D. Map to the four done-means areas

# Sources and gap analysis

Compiled 2026-10-04 by a research pass over the SSI material, the 9/9 webinar, Eric's
March drafts, the Software & Technology framework, and UT's policies. Read-only; no
source was changed. Main finding: the Software & Technology framework fully carries only
SSI Rec 4. The registry note overstated the rest, and **no source addresses
staff-transition continuity** (see D).

Drive folder below = `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\01_PROJECTS\_STALLED\2026-03-05_SSI_PerformanceTechRecs\`
Framework = `~/DEV_archive_hold/2026-10-03/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/` (archive hold until 2026-11-02; repo on GitHub, archived)

## A. Source inventory

| Source | What it is | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Drive `SSI_PerformanceTechRecommendations.pdf` | NCAA CSMAS/SSI, "Performance Technologies Recommendations: Responsible Use in Collegiate Athletics", 5 pp, March 2026, from the May 2025 Summit | Read in full |
| Drive `SSI_Notes_09092026.docx` | Fireflies-style notes on the 9/9 webinar, organised by theme | Read |
| Vault `Inbox/meetings/2026-09-09_NCAA_SSI_Webinar__Performance_Tech__Data_Governance.md` | Summary and action items only | Read |
| Fireflies transcript `01M23EEHZ3CRE03AYYADWA3N0D` | Full 45-min SSI Spotlight webinar | Read in full. A keyword search returned 0 results, but a date-range listing found it. |
| Drive `NCAA_Performance_Tech_Action_Plan_DETAILED.docx` | March 2026, roughly 7.5k words: Baylor roadmap per recommendation, with templates (charter, consent form, access matrix, checklist, surveys) | Read |
| Drive `NCAA_SSI_Summary_and_Recommendations.docx` | Memo dated 7 Mar 2026 with a 4-phase plan (Mar → Fall 2026) | Read (some sentences truncated in the source) |
| Drive `NCAA_PerformanceTech_Condensed_v2.docx` | 1-page table: each recommendation, then a Baylor action | Read (text garbled in places) |
| Drive `SSI_PerformanceTech_StaffOverview_v3.md` | Marp staff deck, April 2026 | Read |
| Vault `Inbox/meetings/2026-05-26_Athlete_Data_Legal_Discussion.md` | Summary of an outside-counsel discussion (proposal for phased policy, vendor-risk, SOP and training work) | Summary only. No transcript found. |
| Framework `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-04-…design.md` | Design document | Read |
| Framework `deliverables/Software_and_Tech_Management_EXEC_SUMMARY_ER_2026-08-14.docx` and `Software_and_Tech_Management_ER_2026-08-14.docx` | 2-page summary and full draft | Read |
| Framework `docs/TALKING_POINTS_ER_2026-08-13_internal.md` | Internal talking points | Read |
| Framework `UT_Technology Policies and Procedures/` SMED-8055 policy, PROC-SMED-8055, SMED-8110 | Peer examples | Read |
| UT `Human Performance Release.pdf` | Scanned image. A 2015-dated **assumption-of-risk / liability waiver**, **not** a data-consent form. | Viewed |

UT's policy lists a "Student-Athlete Informed Consent Form – Performance Technology Use",
but that form is not in the folder.

## B. SSI recommendations (PDF structure)

The PDF uses three kinds of statement (p1, Fig. 1): **Foundational**, **Recommendation**
and **Strategy**.

**Foundational statements (p2)**
- **Fundamentals.**
  - Performance technology is defined broadly: "devices that enable users to collect and record biometric and/or performance data", including "cameras, sensors, surveys, software, mobile apps".
  - It is "just one tool".
  - Quality varies (accuracy, reliability, validity, function) and should be assessed "prior to selecting or implementing".
- **Rights and Protections.**
  - Schools need to understand "student-athlete rights and protections" and "applicable local and international laws".
  - Unintended impacts "including implications for mental health" matter.
- **Written Plan.** Covers how groups are educated, how data is managed, how purchase and implementation decisions are made, and how continuous improvement works.

**Rec 1 – Policy (p3).** Establish a written plan.
- 1.1: a multidisciplinary team develops, "routinely" reviews and revises it (student-athletes, sports medicine, coaches, athletics administration, legal affairs, IT).
- 1.2: address school-specific considerations.

**Rec 2 – Education (p3).** "Education is foundational for informed consent."
- 2.1: "At least once annually" for anyone selecting, using or accessing data.
- 2.2: tailor by group (student-athletes, coaches, S&C, sports medicine, administration).
- 2.3: topics are limitations and harms; data privacy and security; student-athlete rights ("e.g., informed consent"); departmental policies.

**Rec 3 – Data Management (p4).** Establish "who owns data… where and how data is stored,
who has the authority to access data and how data is permitted to be used", working with
legal and risk management.
- 3.1: who may interpret and communicate data, with "required competencies and oversight".
- 3.2: what rights, "if any", the school has over collection, use, access and ownership, "including considerations for transfer student-athletes".
- 3.3: permissible uses. Sports medicine must be involved when data informs medical decisions, preserving the "unchallengeable, autonomous authority" of primary healthcare providers over return-to-play.

**Rec 4 – Selecting and Implementing New Technologies (p4).** A structured decision process.
- 4.1: evidence-based standards for value, usability and quality.
- 4.2: assess accuracy, reliability, validity and function.
- 4.3: a multidisciplinary group decides (sports medicine, sport science, coaching, IT, data security, administration, compliance).

**Rec 5 – Continuous Improvement (p5).** Get feedback "routinely" and revise the plan.
- 5.1: a multidisciplinary group, ideally including the plan's authors.
- 5.2: student-athlete feedback is "critical".
- 5.3: feedback from other groups on implementation, effectiveness and education.

The PDF does **not** mention vendor contracts, NIL, research use or staff turnover.

## C. Webinar takeaways (9/9 SSI Spotlight)

Speakers: the SSI moderator "Dina"; Tim Coffey, Longwood (FAR, biomechanist; the
transcript renders "Crockey"); Mark Koberly, Iowa State Sr. Assoc. AD (the notes spell
it "Coberly").

**Consent**
- **Mark (21:34):** athletes "should have the right to not participate." Some data is unavoidable (venue tracking), but "a wearable… would require their consent", and consent "is one of the things that probably most people are not doing."
- **Tim (02:47):** the summit's origin was athletes opting out of research because "I don't want the number in my head."
- **Mark (34:16):** athletes should be told when their de-identified data goes to vendor norm-building.

**Data ownership and privacy**
- **Tim (30:13):** "talk with your general counsel".
  - State laws vary, and HIPAA has "real exclusions".
  - Staff treat this data as postable "in a locker room" or usable "as part of a broadcast".
  - De-identification fails: with a roster of 13–14, "I can probably identify which athlete's which".
  - Cloud storage risk.
  - Settle access "on the front end before we start collecting".
- **Mark (34:16):** physiological data (HR, HRV) is "more likely to be HIPAA protected" than performance data (40-yard time).
- **Tim (39:45):** "if you're not doing anything with it, don't collect it" (the IRB minimum-data principle).

**Vendor contracts**
- **Moderator (33:09):** vendors offer "a discount if you sell back some of your data". Purchasers may not grasp it, and sports medicine "may not be aware that that is even part of the contract".
- **Mark (34:16):** vendors commonly pool de-identified data "to start developing norms". Involve legal and IT.
- **Moderator (36:16):** add campus risk management.

**NIL / pay**
- **Mark (34:16):** "now that we're paying players… there's going to be a bigger concern" about data use. He cited pro-league player-association rules as precedent.

**Turnover.** Athlete turnover only, not staff. **Tim (38:38):** "with the transfer portal, rosters change over even faster", so feedback and norms need re-checking.

**Governance and adoption**
- **Mark (10:16 / 13:37):** purchases driven by "fear of missing out". Start from the question. Be "data guided, not data driven". Iowa State built "more procedures" than policy, plus an intake **form** asking about validity, reliability, use, access and ownership.
- **Mark (17:35):** two risks: failing to act on critical data, and misuse or misinterpretation.
- **Mark (26:22) / Tim (29:10):** "black box algorithm". Two devices gave "completely different scores" on the same workout, and four published equations exist for one metric.
- **Mark (42:10):** value means ROI; re-evaluate "if we're not acting on the data".

**Mental health**
- **Tim (19:05):** a rugby "data surveillance" study, and staff who could not define acceleration.
- **Mark (26:22):** leaderboards.

## D. Map to the four done-means areas

**1. Technology adoption plan**
- **SSI:** Recs 1 and 4, plus the written-plan foundational statement.
- **March drafts:** extensive.
  - Working Group charter and a 10-section plan outline.
  - Evaluation checklist (10 criteria; minimum 3 on each, average ≥3.5; a score of 1 on security or athlete impact rejects).
  - 30–60-day pilot, 90-day post-implementation review.
  - 6-step purchase flow and a decision log.
  - Their timeline (plan approved June 2026) has lapsed.
- **Framework (08-14):** **fully carries Rec 4.**
  - Idea Form and ATH Form.
  - Business Office, then ITS control points.
  - STRN-based scorecard.
  - Three review levels, an expedited lane, and a trial sandbox (spec).
- **Gaps:**
  - Rec 1's standing multidisciplinary group and the plan's review cycle are "planned for Version 1".
  - The March checklist and the framework scorecard compete and need reconciling.

**2. Athlete consent**
- **SSI:** Rec 2, 2.3, and Rights and Protections. No consent mechanism is prescribed.
- **March drafts:** a full consent-form template (voluntary, withdraw "without penalty or impact on your athletic scholarship, playing time", retention, transfer, contact) and student-athlete talking points.
- **Framework:** a "Student-Athlete **Notice**" (plain-language explanation), which is not consent. OGC/Privacy reviews consent. The consent template is "planned for Version 1". The spec's blanket-for-performance versus per-instance-for-physiologic consent idea **did not make it into the 08-14 document**.
- **Gaps:**
  - Notice versus consent.
  - Which data can be opted out of.
  - Disclosure of vendor norm-pooling.
  - The system of record.
  - Annual re-consent (UT re-consents annually and when a new technology is introduced).

**3. Vendor data contracts**
- **SSI:** only implicit, through Rec 3 / 3.2. The webinar makes it explicit.
- **March drafts:** a vendor contract audit (ownership, storage and jurisdiction, retention and deletion, portability, breach notification) and a "Selling or sharing data with third parties" prohibited use.
- **Framework:** Procurement must cover "ownership, permitted use, storage, access, data sharing, AI training, automated decision-making, downstream sharing, retention, deletion, portability, and breach notification". Level 3 review applies to third-party processing.
- **May legal discussion:** standardise contracts across "over 50 vendors", vendor risk assessments, and a pending outside-counsel proposal.
- **Gaps:**
  - **No step triggers data return or deletion when a product is discontinued** ("Zero occurrences of exit, termination, or offboarding").
  - No standard data addendum or clause library.
  - No audit of existing contracts.

**4. Staff-transition continuity**
- **No source addresses this.**
  - The SSI PDF covers transfer *student-athletes* only (3.2).
  - The webinar covers roster turnover only.
  - The framework has no offboarding step.
- Inferred scaffolding:
  - The March Data Steward role, version control with a central master copy, and a new-hire onboarding module.
  - The framework's request tracker and inventory.
  - The framework's single point of contact, which is itself a key-person dependency (inferred).
- Eric's original content: access revocation, vendor admin account ownership, data custody, and handover.

**Overlap verdict on the registry note:** only partly right.
- **Rec 4 is fully carried.**
- **Rec 5 is only half carried.** Phase 3 is a utilization and renewal review, while SSI's core is stakeholder feedback, and the annual student-athlete survey and Working Group review are "planned for Version 1".
- **Recs 1–3 are pointed at, not delivered.**
- **The spec's data-appendix FAQ is absent from the 08-14 document.** It held Kenny's performance / physiologic / business data taxonomy, coaches receiving summaries only, consent for external sharing, and contractor agreements.

The new document should reference the framework for the request and review process, and
is effectively its "Version 1" content for Recs 1–3 and 5.

**SSI areas outside the four (Eric to decide):**
- Education (Rec 2).
- The feedback half of Rec 5.
- Independent medical authority (3.3).
- Interpretation competencies (3.1).
- Mental-health and unintended impacts.
- Data security and storage.
- Research use: not in the PDF; it appears only in the March draft and Tim's IRB remark, so treat it as inferred.

## E. What UT suggests about document shape

- **Three layers.** A short **policy** (SMED-8055, about 750 words), a separate **procedure** (PROC-SMED-8055), and named **forms** (consent; selection and evaluation checklist). Data protection is a separate policy (SMED-8110).
- **Standard policy template:**
  - Policy, purpose, audience and scope.
  - Definitions (lifted almost verbatim from SSI).
  - Responsibilities.
  - Procedure pointer, then forms, related information, history, contacts, and approval authorities.
- **Ownership is split.** Applied Sports Science has "day-to-day administrative oversight"; the Chief Medical Officer is policy owner and holds medical data and return-to-play authority. A Performance Technology Committee reviews "at least annually".
- **The procedure mirrors the SSI headings one to one,** and is thin (about 650 words).
- **Contrast with Baylor.** UT chose formal policy. Framework spec open decision #7: the 2026-07-30 meeting preferred "flexible best-practice documents over rigid formal policy".

## F. Open questions (Chris, Legal, Compliance, IT)

1. Best-practice guidance or departmental policy? Who signs, and who is policy owner?
2. What is the Software & Technology framework's status? Is the new document its Version 1, or separate?
3. Data ownership: institution-owned with athlete access (the March draft) or athlete-owned for physiologic data (the spec)?
4. Consent model: blanket or per-instance; opt-out-able data; system of record; re-consent cadence. Notice plus consent, or notice only?
5. How is physiologic versus performance data classified under HIPAA, FERPA and Texas law?
6. Vendor contracts:
   - Standard data addendum?
   - Who audits the roughly 50 contracts?
   - Are data-for-discount and norm-pooling terms allowed?
   - What is the exit and deletion obligation?
7. Was the May outside-counsel proposal received or acted on? (Eric's action item.)
8. Staff transitions: vendor admin account ownership, access revocation, and the data custodian on departure.
9. Retention periods, and the transfer-athlete protocol (the March draft: nothing is sent without the athlete's written request).
10. A standing working group with student-athlete members? Does Rec 2 education ride on existing compliance and orientation sessions?

# SSI crosswalk: Draft v1 of the guide

Every statement in the NCAA SSI *Performance Technologies Recommendations: Responsible
Use in Collegiate Athletics* (CSMAS/SSI, March 2026), mapped to the section or appendix of
`deliverables/SSI_BestPractices_GUIDE_DRAFTv1_ER_2026-10-04` that meets it. SSI item text
is summarised from `docs/SOURCES.md` § B. Status: **Met** = the guide carries it in full;
**Met, pending** = carried, but a position in it waits on the review named in
`docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md`.

Guide sections: 0 Purpose and scope · 1 Governance · 2 Technology adoption · 3 Athlete
consent and education · 4 Data management · 5 Vendor data contracts · 6 Staff-transition
continuity · 7 Continuous improvement. Appendices: A Consent · B Vendor checklist ·
C Offboarding · D Annual review · E Technology intake.

## Foundational statements (SSI p2)

| SSI item | What SSI asks | Where the guide meets it | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 Fundamentals: broad definition | Performance technology covers devices, cameras, sensors, surveys, software and apps | §0 Definitions (SSI definition adopted verbatim in substance; scope lists video, surveys and apps) | Met |
| F1 Fundamentals: "just one tool" | Technology supports, never replaces, professional judgment | §0 Principles ("data guided, not data driven"); §4.4 interpretation rule | Met |
| F1 Fundamentals: quality varies | Assess accuracy, reliability, validity, function before selecting | §2 and Appendix E (gates and rated features) | Met |
| F2 Rights and protections | Know student-athlete rights, local and international law; watch for unintended impacts including mental health | §3 (notice vs consent, rights list), §3.5 education topics, §4.1 legal basis including international law, §7 survey items on harm; Appendix A rights section | Met, pending (OGC: legal classification) |
| F3 Written plan | A plan for education, data management, purchase decisions and continuous improvement | The guide itself, with §1 naming owner, review and version control | Met, pending (Chris: owner and sign-off) |

## Recommendation 1: Policy

| SSI item | What SSI asks | Where the guide meets it | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rec 1 | Establish a written plan | The guide (§0–§7) plus forms A–E | Met |
| 1.1 | Multidisciplinary team, including student-athletes, develops and routinely reviews the plan | §1.1 Working Group membership (two student-athletes, Athletic Medicine, Athletic Performance, coaches, administration, OGC, ITS, Compliance); §1.3 annual review; Appendix D | Met, pending (Chris: charter the group) |
| 1.2 | Address school-specific considerations | §0 "How Baylor already works"; Baylor systems table in §4.2; tech inventory figures in §5.3; framework routing in §2 | Met |

## Recommendation 2: Education

| SSI item | What SSI asks | Where the guide meets it | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rec 2 | Routine education; foundational for informed consent | §3.5 Education, placed inside the consent section on purpose | Met |
| 2.1 | At least once a year for anyone selecting, using or accessing data | §3.5 calendar (annual staff session, orientation, preseason refresher, new-hire onboarding within 30 days); attendance tracked; Appendix D input | Met |
| 2.2 | Tailor by group | §3.5 audience table (student-athletes, coaches, Athletic Performance, Athletic Medicine, administration, ITS) | Met |
| 2.3 | Topics: limitations and harms; privacy and security; rights including consent; departmental policies | §3.5 four required topics, covered in every audience module | Met |

## Recommendation 3: Data management

| SSI item | What SSI asks | Where the guide meets it | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rec 3 | Establish ownership, storage, access and permitted use, with legal and risk management | §4.1 ownership; §4.2 storage and systems; §4.3 access matrix; §4.5 permitted and prohibited uses | Met, pending (Chris/OGC: ownership) |
| 3.1 | Who may interpret and communicate data; competencies and oversight | §4.4 interpretation competencies by data class; Data Steward role in §1.2 | Met |
| 3.2 | The school's rights over collection, use, access and ownership, including transfer athletes | §4.1 ownership position; §4.6 transfer protocol (built on the VALD records-release precedent); Appendix A | Met, pending (OGC: ownership, retention) |
| 3.3 | Permissible uses; Athletic Medicine involved in medical decisions; autonomous authority over return to play | §1.4 medical authority statement; §4.5 permitted uses; Level 3 review routes physiologic data to Athletic Medicine (§2) | Met |

## Recommendation 4: Selecting and implementing new technologies

| SSI item | What SSI asks | Where the guide meets it | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rec 4 | A structured decision process | §2 points to the Software and Technology Management Framework (three phases, two control points, three review levels) | Met, pending (Chris: framework treated as live) |
| 4.1 | Evidence-based standards for value, usability and quality | §2.2 single scoring instrument (Appendix E), built from the STRN Quality Framework and the March checklist | Met |
| 4.2 | Assess accuracy, reliability, validity and function | Appendix E rated features and decision rule; §2.3 trial and 90-day review | Met |
| 4.3 | Multidisciplinary group decides | §1.1 Working Group decides every Level 2 and 3 request; decision recorded on Appendix E; §2.1 reviewers by level | Met |

## Recommendation 5: Continuous improvement

| SSI item | What SSI asks | Where the guide meets it | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rec 5 | Routinely get feedback and revise the plan | §7 annual cycle; Appendix D | Met |
| 5.1 | Multidisciplinary group plans, collects and interprets feedback, ideally the plan's authors | §7.1 Working Group runs the cycle; §1.3 | Met |
| 5.2 | Student-athlete feedback is critical | §7.2 annual survey, SAAC focus group, confidential concern channel, results shared back | Met |
| 5.3 | Feedback from other groups on implementation, effectiveness and education | §7.3 staff survey; technology-by-technology review tied to framework Phase 3; education effectiveness | Met |

## Where Baylor goes beyond SSI

SSI does not mention these. The guide adds them because the 9/9 SSI webinar, the tech
inventory, or Baylor's own experience made the case.

| Topic | Guide section | Why it is in |
|---|---|---|
| Vendor data contracts: ownership, exit and deletion, AI training, data-for-discount and norm pooling | §5, Appendix B | Webinar (Moderator 33:09; Koberly 34:16): purchasers and Athletic Medicine may not know a contract trades data for price. 75 of 188 inventoried products handle athlete data. No current Baylor step requires data return or deletion when a product is dropped. |
| Staff-transition continuity | §6, Appendix C | No external source covers it. Baylor's own pipelines (GPS, force plate, VALD, RTP reports) are built and run by a small number of people. |
| NIL and pay | §4.5 prohibited uses; Appendix A consent row | Webinar (Koberly 34:16): paying players raises the stakes on data use. |
| Research use | §4.5; Appendix A consent row | Only with IRB approval and separate consent; the "don't collect it if you don't use it" rule (Coffey 39:45). |
| Physiologic vs performance data classes | §4.2, §4.3 | Webinar (Koberly 34:16): physiologic data is more likely to be protected health information. |
| Algorithm transparency ("black box") | Appendix E gate; Appendix B row 12 | Webinar (Koberly 26:22, Coffey 29:10): two devices gave different scores for the same session. |

## Coverage check

24 SSI items (5 foundational, 5 recommendations, 14 strategies). 24 mapped, 0 unmapped.

"""Appendix forms A-E for the Performance Technology Best Practices guide.

Imported by build_guide.py; each function returns a finished BaylorDoc.
Keep form content here and guide content in build_guide.py.
"""
from baylor_docstyle import BaylorDoc

STATUS = "Draft v1 for discussion"
BOX = "☐"


def _head(title, deck, use):
    d = BaylorDoc(title, deck=deck, status=STATUS)
    d.meta([
        ["Status", "**Draft v1** for discussion. Pending review as marked."],
        ["Date", "October 4, 2026"],
        ["Used by", use],
        ["Owner", "Performance Technology Working Group"],
        ["Prepared by", "Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics"],
        ["Companions", "Performance Technology Best Practices (the guide); Appendices A to E"],
    ])
    return d


def consent_form():
    d = _head("Appendix A: Student-Athlete Performance Technology Consent",
              "What Baylor Athletics collects with performance technology, why, who sees it, "
              "and what you can say yes or no to.",
              "Every student-athlete, at the start of each academic year and whenever a new "
              "technology is introduced in their sport. Kept by Athletic Medicine.")
    d.callout("Read this first",
              "Some data is collected from every athlete in a team setting and cannot be "
              "switched off, such as venue tracking and video of practice. You are told about "
              "it here (Part 2). Other data needs your yes before it is collected (Part 3). "
              "Saying no to anything in Part 3 has **no effect on your scholarship, playing "
              "time or place on the team.** [Pending OGC: final consent and notice language.]")

    d.section("Who you are")
    d.table(["Field", "Entry"], [
        ["Name", ""], ["Sport", ""], ["Academic year", ""],
        ["This form is", f"{BOX} Annual consent    {BOX} New technology added    {BOX} Change of consent"],
    ], widths=[1.8, 4.9])

    d.section("Notice: data collected in team settings")
    d.para("These are part of normal team activity. You can ask to see your own data at any time.")
    d.table(["Technology (examples)", "What it records", "Who sees it"], [
        ["Video of practice and competition", "Movement, technique, tactics", "Coaches, Athletic Performance, Applied Performance, Athletic Medicine"],
        ["Team GPS or venue tracking (e.g. Catapult, Kinexon)", "Distance, speed, accelerations, training load", "Athletic Performance and Applied Performance; coaches see summaries"],
        ["Force plate and jump testing (e.g. VALD ForceDecks)", "Jump height, force, asymmetry, readiness", "Athletic Performance and Applied Performance; Athletic Medicine for injury and return to play"],
        ["Wellness check-ins", "Sleep, soreness, stress", "Athletic Medicine; Athletic Performance and coaches see flags only"],
    ], widths=[2.2, 2.0, 2.5])
    d.note("The list for your sport is attached by your sport's Athletic Performance coach. "
           "[Pending OGC: whether team GPS and testing sit under notice or consent.]")

    d.section("Consent: data that needs your yes")
    d.table(["Item", "Yes", "No"], [
        ["Wearables worn outside team sessions (heart rate, HRV, sleep rings or straps)", BOX, BOX],
        ["Body composition testing (DEXA or similar)", BOX, BOX],
        ["Cognitive testing (e.g. S2 Cognition)", BOX, BOX],
        ["Use of my de-identified data by a vendor to build norms or improve products", BOX, BOX],
        ["Being asked to take part in research using my data. Each study still needs IRB approval and its own consent form.", BOX, BOX],
        ["Sharing my individual data with anyone outside Baylor Athletics (for example a new school, a pro team, an agent or an NIL partner). Each release still needs a separate written request from me.", BOX, BOX],
    ], widths=[5.3, 0.7, 0.7])

    d.section("Your rights")
    d.bullets([
        "You can see your own data, and ask for a copy, at any time.",

        "Medicine or the Data Steward in writing. Collection stops from that date.",

        "written request.",

        "[Pending OGC: retention period.] You may ask for earlier deletion when you leave, "
        "where the law allows.",

        "tell Athletic Medicine, the Data Steward or a SAAC representative.",
    ])

           "student-athlete's Athletic Medicine file. [Pending Athletic Medicine: system of record.]")
    return d

              "The terms every contract must cover before a vendor holds Baylor athlete data.",

              "uses it for the contract audit.")

    d.section("Required terms")
    d.para("Mark each term Met, Not met, or N/A. Any **Not met** in rows 1 to 6 sends the "
           "contract back to the vendor before signature or renewal. N/A on rows 1 to 6 is "
           "allowed only with a written reason approved by OGC and attached to this checklist.")
    rows = [
        ["1", "Ownership", "Baylor owns the data. The vendor has no rights beyond delivering the service. [Pending Chris/OGC: ownership position.]"],

        ["3", "Exit: return and deletion", "When the contract ends or the product is dropped, the vendor returns all data in a standard format within 30 days, then deletes it and certifies deletion in writing."],

    d.table(["#", "Term", "What the contract must say", "Met / Not met / N/A"],

        "**Decline or renegotiate:** any gate fails.",

    d.table(["Reviewer", "Name", "Date"], [

357	           "leaves. At Baylor this is a real exposure. Much of the department's performance "
358	           "data flows through pipelines that a small number of Applied Performance staff "
359	           "built and run: the GPS report pipeline, the force plate database and its "
360	           "scheduled refresh, the VALD workbook, the return-to-play reports. Some of that work "
361	           "sits on one machine or under individual accounts. A departure "
362	           "mid-season can stop these systems when they are most needed. The rules below make every system survive the departure of the "
363	           "person who knows it best.")
364	    d.subhead("6.1  Institutional accounts")
365	    d.para("Every vendor platform's admin account belongs to a Baylor institutional address or "
366	           "a shared departmental mailbox, never to an individual's personal or Baylor email. "
367	           "Code, scripts, report templates and scheduled jobs live in Baylor-owned locations "
368	           "and run under service accounts where ITS allows. Existing platforms are moved over "
369	           "during the contract audit (Section 5.3). [Pending ITS: shared mailbox and "
370	           "service-account options.]")
371	    d.subhead("6.2  A custodian and a backup for every platform")
372	    d.para("Each platform in the inventory has a named custodian and a named backup. The backup "
373	           "can log in, run a normal report end to end, and knows where credentials are held. "
374	           "The custodian also keeps the vendor contact, renewal date and licence count "
375	           "current in the inventory.")
376	    d.subhead("6.3  Handover notes")
377	    d.para("For each system a person runs, they keep a one-page note: what it does, how data "
378	           "gets in, how reports are built and sent and to whom, where credentials are, and "
379	           "known problems. It is updated when the system changes, not written in the last week.")
380	    d.subhead("6.4  Departure")
381	    d.para("When a staff member who uses or runs performance technology gives notice, the "
382	           "supervisor and Data Steward start Appendix C. Access is removed on every platform "
383	           "on the last working day, shared credentials and API keys are rotated, local copies "
384	           "of athlete data are returned or deleted with written confirmation, and the backup "
385	           "proves they can run each system before sign-off. The same checklist applies to "
386	           "interns and contractors. [Pending ITS: access-removal timeline.]")
387	
388	    # 7 -------------------------------------------------------------------
389	    d.section("7.  Continuous improvement", numbered=False)
390	    d.subhead("7.1  The annual cycle (SSI Rec 5, 5.1)")
391	    d.para("Each spring the Working Group, which includes the people who wrote this guide, "
392	           "gathers the year's feedback and reviews every technology, the education program "
393	           "and the guide itself with Appendix D. It ends with a decision for each "
394	           "technology (continue, modify or stop), a revised guide, and a one-page report to "
395	           "the document owner. The technology reviews line up with the framework's Phase 3 "
396	           "usage review, so a product is not judged twice.")
397	    d.subhead("7.2  Student-athlete feedback (SSI Rec 5.2)")
398	    d.bullets([
399	        "A short annual survey (about 13 questions) at the end of the spring semester: whether "
400	        "athletes understand what is collected and who sees it, whether they feel free to say "
401	        "no, whether the technology helped, and how often data caused them stress or anxiety.",
402	        "One SAAC focus group each year, across sports.",
403	        "A confidential channel for concerns at any time, through the Data Steward or a SAAC "
404	        "representative, open from spring 2027.",
405	        "Results and the changes made are reported back to athletes through SAAC.",
406	    ])
407	    d.subhead("7.3  Staff and effectiveness feedback (SSI Rec 5.3)")
408	    d.para("A short staff survey covers reliability, training and usefulness. Each technology is "
409	           "checked against the question it was bought to answer, using utilization data from "
410	           "the framework's Phase 3 review: if we are not acting on the data, we stop "
411	           "collecting it or stop paying for it. Education is judged on attendance and on "
412	           "what the surveys show people still do not know.")
413	    d.subhead("Timeline to in use")
414	    d.table(["By", "Step"], [
415	        ["Oct 14, 2026", "Plan agreed with Chris; three decisions settled"],
416	        ["Oct 24, 2026", "Input from OGC, Procurement, ITS, Athletic Medicine"],
417	        ["Nov 6, 2026", "First draft to Chris (this document, revised)"],
418	        ["Nov 25, 2026", "Final; consent form reviewed by OGC; Appendix C reviewed by ITS"],
419	        ["Dec 16, 2026", "In use: Working Group meeting set; consent ready for spring"],
420	        ["Spring 2027", "First surveys and first annual review"],
421	    ], widths=[1.3, 5.4])
422	    d.note("Sources: NCAA SSI Performance Technologies Recommendations (March 2026); NCAA SSI "
423	           "webinar on performance technology and data governance (September 9, 2026); Applied "
424	           "Performance action plan drafts (March 2026); Software and Technology Management "
425	           "Framework draft and Technology Evaluation Scorecard (August 2026); Baylor Athletics "
426	           "technology inventory findings (September 16, 2026; final October 1, 2026), the source "
427	           "for product, unit and retirement counts; Applied Performance VALD transfer-data "
428	           "records (2026); UT Austin SMED-8055 for structure.")
429	    return d
